title: Alia Bhatt Just Gave the Spy Universe Its First Heroine. The Box Office Isn't Sure What to Do with Her.
excerpt: Alpha opened to ₹34 crore net — the weakest debut in YRF's spy franchise. But the daily growth tells a more interesting story.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Alpha opened with ₹34 crore net, the weakest debut in YRF's Spy Universe.
  • The film showed daily growth, indicating positive word of mouth.
  • Over 608,000 tickets sold on BookMyShow during the opening weekend.
  • Alpha's performance is crucial for the future of female-led films in the franchise.
  • The film's urban audience engagement suggests a shift in demographics.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=rVK4pOPATiI The numbers are in, and they're complicated. **Alpha**, the first female-led film in Yash Raj Films' blockbuster Spy Universe, wrapped its opening weekend with ₹34 crore net at the domestic box office and an estimated ₹58.80 crore worldwide. By any normal Bollywood standard, that's a solid debut. By the standard of the franchise that gave us **Pathaan** (₹280 crore opening weekend) and **War 2** (₹175 crore), it's the quietest entrance the Spy Universe has ever made. But here's the thing about Alpha — it grew every single day. ## The Weekend, Day by Day Friday landed at ₹9.25 crore net across 7,534 shows, with occupancy hovering around 20%. Not the explosive start fans expected. Saturday climbed 24% to ₹11.50 crore, with occupancy rising to 25%. And Sunday pushed further to ₹13.25 crore — a 15% jump — with peak-hour occupancy hitting nearly 50% in markets like Hyderabad. That's the kind of upward trajectory that suggests word of mouth is working, even if the initial rush wasn't there. > **"Saturday climbed 24% to ₹11.50 crore, with occupancy rising to 25%."** > "I've always known you're an extraordinary actor. But this journey made me fall in love with the artist you are." — Aditya Dhar, on a different YRF universe star this weekend Director **Shiv Rawail** has put **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari Wagh** at the centre of a high-octane espionage thriller that also features **Bobby Deol** as the antagonist and — in what's become the biggest talking point — a **Hrithik Roshan** cameo reprising Major Kabir from the War films. That cameo, along with Alia's stylish entry sequence, has been the single most discussed element of the film online. https://www.instagram.com/p/DaQcmVYk8Of/ ![Spy Universe — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/d6/YRF_Spy_Universe_logo.jpg) ## Where It Played Best The NCR led the charge with 739 shows and 33% occupancy, followed by Mumbai at 27.3% and Bengaluru at an impressive 31.3%. Hyderabad punched above its weight with 31.8% occupancy despite fewer screens, hitting 49% during evening shows. The film clearly skews urban and multiplex — which is exactly where diaspora audiences tend to be most engaged. Overseas, Alpha collected an estimated ₹18 crore gross over the weekend, with North America contributing significantly. For NRIs who've followed every instalment of the Spy Universe — from **Ek Tha Tiger** to **Tiger Zinda Hai** to **Pathaan** — this is the franchise's most ambitious departure yet. ## The Franchise Comparison That Matters

Here's how Alpha stacks up against every other YRF Spy Universe opening weekend (India net): - **Pathaan**: ₹280.75 crore (Wednesday release) - **War 2**: ₹175.75 crore (Thursday release) - **War**: ₹166.25 crore (Wednesday release) - **Tiger Zinda Hai**: ₹114.93 crore (Friday release) - **Ek Tha Tiger**: ₹100.57 crore (Wednesday release) - **Tiger 3**: ₹44.50 crore (Sunday release) - **Alpha**: ₹34.00 crore (Friday release) It's dead last. But context matters: Alpha didn't have a holiday release window (Pathaan had Republic Day, War 2 had Diwali), and it's the first film in the franchise without a male superstar as the primary draw. Alia Bhatt is a massive name, but the action-thriller audience in India still leans heavily male, and converting that demographic to a female-led spy film was always going to be the real mission. ## The Bigger Question Over 608,000 tickets were sold on BookMyShow alone across the weekend. The film held 21,855 shows in three days. These aren't the numbers of a film that's being ignored — they're the numbers of a film that's finding its audience slower than the franchise is used to. Monday's hold will be the real tell. If Alpha drops sharply on the first weekday, the theatrical run becomes a fight for respectability. If it holds — even at ₹5-6 crore — there's a genuine path to ₹75-80 crore lifetime domestically.
Audience Engagement Insights
›608,000 tickets sold on BookMyShow.
›21,855 shows held over the weekend.
›NCR led with 33% occupancy.
›Hyderabad peaked at 49% during evening shows.
For YRF, the stakes go beyond one film's P&L. Alpha is the proof of concept for whether the Spy Universe can survive without Salman, Shah Rukh, or Hrithik carrying the poster. The answer, so far, is: yes, but it's a harder sell. Alia and Sharvari have delivered the goods on screen. Now the box office needs to catch up. *Alpha is currently playing in theatres worldwide, including across North America, the UK, and the Middle East.*
